claims.text: Introducing yttrium oxide nanoparticles into a high-entropy-alloy coating will improve its wear resistance.
The proposed improvement will hold from 20°C to 500°C under a contact pressure of 1 GPa and a sliding speed of 1 m/s.
The introduced yttrium oxide nanoparticles will be dispersed within the high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Yttrium oxide nanoparticles will act as pinning points for dislocations.
Dislocation pinning by the nanoparticles will reduce dislocation mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility will reduce coating wear.
Yttrium oxide nanoparticles will deflect crack-propagation paths.
Crack deflection by the nanoparticles will inhibit the formation of large cracks.
The modified coating will have a wear rate 20% lower than that of an otherwise identical unmodified coating.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on nanoparticle size, distribution, and amount, as well as on the specific high-entropy-alloy composition.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing modified and unmodified coatings in a pin-on-disk wear test using a steel ball as the counterbody.
Wear rate, coefficient of friction, and surface roughness will be measured.
The hypothesis is falsified if the modified coating's wear rate is not significantly lower than that of the unmodified coating.
